# frontier-connector-arrays

Reads NetCDF 3/4, generic HDF5 and Zarr v2/v3. Common layouts are detected automatically; any other layout takes a mapping config.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install arrays
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info arrays
```

## Status

**`hdf5`** (`verified-public-sample`): Detects datasets with dimension scales, The Well, PDEBench / FNO-style grids and points + cells mesh layouts. Any other layout needs a mapping config: the error prints the dataset tree and a mapping skeleton. The Well, dimension-scale and mesh layouts are validated on generated files only. Fluent CFF, CGNS, MATLAB v7.3, VTKHDF, Exodus, XDMF heavy data, MED and PyFR files belong to their own connectors.

**`netcdf`** (`verified-public-sample`): NetCDF-4 is read with h5py, NetCDF-3 classic and 64-bit-offset with scipy (memory-mapped). CF grids with 1-D coordinates and UGRID 2-D face meshes are detected automatically. Curvilinear grids, CDF-5, UGRID 1-D / 3-D-layered and DSG feature types need a mapping or options={'engine': 'xarray'}.

**`zarr`** (`verified-synthetic`): Reads directory and .zip stores in Zarr v2 and v3. Dimension names come from _ARRAY_DIMENSIONS (v2) or dimension_names (v3); CF attributes are honoured as for NetCDF. Remote stores (s3://, gs://) are not opened. Validated on generated files only.

## Getting the data out

**`hdf5`**: Write the arrays with h5py / HDF5 from any solver or script, then describe the layout with a mapping config (--mapping file.json) unless it is one of the auto-detected layouts (dimension scales, PDEBench, The Well, points+cells+fields).

**`netcdf`**: Most climate/ocean/weather models and many CFD codes write NetCDF directly; from Python use xarray.Dataset.to_netcdf, from ParaView/VisIt use the NetCDF writer. OPeNDAP URLs, GRIB and multi-file datasets go through options={'engine': 'xarray'}.

**`zarr`**: xarray: Dataset.to_zarr(path). Any zarr group written by a solver or script can be described with a mapping config. A frontier-dataset directory (or one of its sample stores) is read back as-is.

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0. Installs `h5py>=3.10`, `scipy>=1.13`, `zarr>=3.0`.

| Optional package | Licence | Used to | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xarray` | Apache-2.0 | open GRIB, OPeNDAP and multi-file datasets (engine=xarray) |  |

plugins.readme:
# frontier-connector-catalyst

Reads Conduit Mesh Blueprint steps from a spool directory, Conduit relay files or ADIOS2 (BP5 / SST), during or after the run. Not validated against ParaView Catalyst.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install catalyst
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info catalyst
```

A running solver feeds a Frontier dataset step by step. The unit of exchange is the Conduit Mesh
Blueprint tree, the same tree a ParaView Catalyst 2 adaptor passes under
`catalyst/channels/<name>/data`.

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors import catalyst run/spool --out dataset --option timeout=600
python -m frontier_connectors import catalyst run/spool --out dataset --dry-run
python -m frontier_connectors convert run/spool --out dataset      # after the run
```

## What it reads

| Source | Written by | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| spool directory, `frontier-spool` v1 (`frontier-stream.json`, `step_<n>.npz`, `frontier-stream.done`) | `frontier_emit.py` in the solver or in the Catalyst pipeline script, both in `exporter-catalyst` | numpy |
| Conduit relay Blueprint series (`<name>.cycle_<n>.root` + domain files; hdf5, json, yaml, conduit_json, conduit_base64_json, conduit_bin) | `conduit.relay.io.blueprint.save_mesh`, Ascent relay extracts | `h5py` for hdf5, `pyyaml` for yaml; Conduit itself is not needed |
| ADIOS2 BP4 / BP5 file (also while written) or SST stream | variables named by Blueprint path, or the Fides predefined-model attributes | `adios2` (Apache-2.0) |
| `conduit.Node` or nested `dict` in memory | `frontier_connector_catalyst.blueprint.mesh_to_samples`, `StepConverter` | LLNL Conduit only for `Node` objects |

Files a Catalyst pipeline writes with plain VTK extractors (`.vtpd`, `.vtm`, VTKHDF) are read by
the `vtk` connector.

## Blueprint coverage

- Coordsets: `uniform`, `rectilinear`, `explicit` (Cartesian).
- Topologies: `points`, `uniform`, `rectilinear`, `structured`, `unstructured` with
  `point line tri quad tet hex wedge pyramid`, `polygonal`, `polyhedral` (with `subelements`) and
  `mixed` (`shape_map`).
- Fields: `vertex` or `element`, scalar or mcarray, `units`.
- `state/{time,cycle,domain_id}`, multi-domain trees, Catalyst `mesh` and `multimesh` channels.

Uniform and rectilinear topologies become `grid` samples, all-2-D topologies `surface`
(triangulated, cell data follows), point topologies `point_cloud`, the rest `mesh`. One zone per
(domain, topology); MPI-decomposed domains stay separate zones.

Not supported: non-Cartesian coordsets, strided structured topologies, high-order meshes and
fields. Skipped with a warning: material fields, matsets, specsets, adjsets, nestsets.

## Following a live stream

`--option follow=true` (the importer's default) tails the source. Each step is yielded once, in
increasing step number, and only when complete; the dataset is appended along time.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `timeout` | 60 | seconds without a new complete step before giving up; also the wait for the stream to appear |
| `poll` | 0.2 | seconds between looks |
| `until` | `done-marker` | `timeout`: ignore end markers, stop after `timeout` idle seconds (relay series) |
| `on_timeout` | `stop` | keep what arrived; `error` raises and leaves no dataset |
| `on_restart` | `skip` | steps re-emitted after a restart from a checkpoint are not read twice; `error` raises |
| `order_grace` | 2 | seconds to wait for a step the producer's `prev` chain says is missing |
| `partial_grace` | 5 | seconds an unreadable visible file may stay unchanged before it is declared corrupt |
| `settle` | 0.5 | seconds a relay file must be unmodified before it is read |
| `max_steps` | - | stop after N steps |
| `geometry` | `changed` | `always` sends the mesh with every step (needed with `--time-as-samples` for changing topology) |
| `name` | - | relay series base name when a directory holds several |
| `engine`, `adios_parameters`, `fides_order` | `BPFile`, -, `zyx` | ADIOS2 engine (`BP5`, `BP4`, `SST`), engine parameters, grid array order of Fides models |

While following, `--times` accepts `all` or a forward range `start:stop:step`. Timeouts,
restarts, lost steps and failed end markers are logged and added to the conversion warnings.
Hidden `.<name>.tmp-<pid>` files are never read. A visible file that does not decode is retried.

## ADIOS2 variable convention

Each Blueprint array is a variable named by its path (`coordsets/coords/values/x`,
`topologies/mesh/elements/connectivity`, `fields/T/values`, `state/time`, `state/cycle`), and
each string leaf an attribute (`topologies/mesh/type = "unstructured"`,
`fields/T/association = "vertex"`, `fields/T/units = "K"`). The mesh may be written in the first
step only. Several domains share a prefix (`fluid/coordsets/...`). The attributes
`frontier/solver`, `frontier/solver_version`, `frontier/domain` and `frontier/time_units` go to
the dataset metadata. The Fides predefined models `uniform`, `rectilinear`,
`unstructured_single` and `unstructured` are translated; the Fides JSON file, XGC and GTC are not.

## Status

`verified-synthetic`. Reads frontier-spool directories, Conduit relay Blueprint files (hdf5, json, yaml, conduit_*) and ADIOS2 BP4 / BP5 files and BP5 / SST streams, during or after the run. Validated with Conduit 0.9.5 and ADIOS2 2.12.1. Not validated against ParaView Catalyst (the pipeline script), Fides or MPI-parallel writers.

## Getting the data out

Get the solver-side scripts with `python -m frontier_connectors plugins install exporter-catalyst`, then use one of: (1) copy frontier_emit.py (numpy only) next to the solver and call Emitter.write_step(step, time, blueprint_mesh) at each output step; (2) run the Catalyst 2 pipeline frontier_catalyst_pipeline.py (CATALYST_IMPLEMENTATION_NAME=paraview), which writes the same spool; (3) write Conduit relay Blueprint files (relay.io.blueprint.save_mesh, Ascent) or ADIOS2 BP5 / SST with Blueprint paths as variable names. Follow the run with `python -m frontier_connectors import catalyst <spool|stream> --out ds`. Files a Catalyst pipeline writes with plain VTK extractors (.vtpd / .vtm series, VTKHDF) are read by the `vtk` connector.

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0.

| Optional package | Licence | Used to | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `adios2` | Apache-2.0 | read ADIOS2 BP4/BP5 files and follow BP5/SST streams |  |
| `h5py` | BSD-3-Clause | read Conduit relay Blueprint files written with the hdf5 protocol |  |
| `pyyaml` | MIT | read Conduit relay Blueprint files written with the yaml protocol |  |
| `conduit` | BSD-3-Clause | pass conduit.Node objects to the Blueprint bridge directly | LLNL Conduit is not on PyPI (the PyPI project named conduit is unrelated): build it from https://github.com/LLNL/conduit or use Spack |

# frontier-connector-cgns

Reads CGNS/HDF5 with h5py and ADF files through VTK.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install cgns
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info cgns
```

## Status

`verified-public-sample`. Reads CGNS/HDF5 with h5py: structured and unstructured zones, linear and quadratic elements, MIXED, NGON_n / NFACE_n, boundary patches as surface zones, vertex and cell-centred solutions, rind, links, FlowSolutionPointers, file-per-step series, units, reference state and flow equations. Cubic and higher elements, face-centred solutions and non-Cartesian coordinates are not supported. ADF files and options={'engine': 'vtk'} go through VTK's vtkCGNSReader, without the CGNS metadata.

## Getting the data out

Export CGNS from the solver or post-processor (Ansys CFX: cfx5export -cgns; Fluent: File > Export > CGNS; STAR-CCM+: File > Export > CGNS; Fidelity/FINE, SU2, elsA, Pointwise write it natively) and point at the .cgns file or a directory holding a numbered series.

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0. Installs `h5py>=3.10`, `vtk>=9.3`.

plugins.readme:
# frontier-exporter-catalyst

A numpy-only step emitter, a ParaView Catalyst 2 pipeline script and adaptor notes that run next to the solver and write what the catalyst connector reads. The pipeline script is not validated against ParaView.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install exporter-catalyst
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info exporter-catalyst
```

Copy the scripts next to a case:

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install-exporter catalyst --to <dir>
```

Files: `README.txt`, `adaptor_example.txt`, `frontier_catalyst_pipeline.py`, `frontier_emit.py`. Usage is in `README.txt`.

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `frontier_emit.py` | numpy-only emitter of the `frontier-spool` protocol: atomic step files, header, end marker, restart support, mesh builders. It imports nothing from Frontier; copy it into the solver repository. |
| `frontier_catalyst_pipeline.py` | ParaView Catalyst 2 pipeline script. `--mode spool` converts a channel's VTK data to Blueprint and emits it (serial); `--mode vtk` adds a VTPD extractor (parallel; read with the `vtk` connector). Not validated against ParaView. |
| `adaptor_example.txt` | the Conduit node a Catalyst 2 adaptor passes (C++, Fortran, Python), `CATALYST_IMPLEMENTATION_NAME` / `CATALYST_IMPLEMENTATION_PATHS`, other transports |

```python
from frontier_emit import Emitter, uniform_mesh

with Emitter("spool", solver="my-solver") as out:  # writes the end marker on exit
    for step in range(n_steps):
        ...
        out.write_step(step, t, uniform_mesh((nx, ny), spacing=(dx, dy), point_fields={"T": T}))
```

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors import catalyst spool --out dataset      # while the solver runs
```

## Status

`frontier_emit.py` is validated. The Catalyst pipeline script is not validated against ParaView.

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0.

Reads STL, OBJ, PLY and OFF surfaces. STEP, IGES and BREP need an optional tessellator (cadquery-ocp, or gmsh).

plugins.readme:
# frontier-connector-meshio

Reads Exodus II, XDMF, Gmsh MSH and MED files, SU2 meshes, and the other mesh formats meshio supports.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install meshio
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info meshio
```

## Status

**`exodus`** (`verified-public-sample`): Element blocks are the default zones; side sets and node sets are extra zones. Reads nodal, element and global variables at all time steps. One piece of a parallel decomposition is read as it is, without merging.

**`gmsh`** (`verified-public-sample`): Physical groups become zones. $NodeData and $ElementData views are read, including several time steps of one view; element views assume the consecutive element tags Gmsh writes. $ElementNodeData and .pos parsed views are not read. MSH 4 files need every saved entity in a physical group. Views and binary files are validated on generated files only.

**`med`** (`verified-public-sample`): Groups (families) become zones; node groups are point-cloud zones. Reads fields on nodes and cells for every stored time step. Gauss-point (ELGA) and element-node (ELNO) fields are averaged per cell; their storage order for more than one cell is not validated on a real file. Fields on a profile are NaN outside it. Structured MED meshes and polyhedra are not read. Several time steps are validated on generated files only.

**`meshio`** (`verified-public-sample`): Reads Medit .mesh / .meshb, Netgen .vol, TetGen .node / .ele, UGRID and FLAC3D .f3grid. Region and material ids become zones. MOAB .h5m, DOLFIN XML, AVS-UCD, PERMAS, Kratos .mdpa and HMF are validated on meshio-written files only.

**`su2`** (`verified-public-sample`): Reads the mesh, markers as boundary zones and multi-zone meshes; solver, turbulence model, free-stream parameters and the boundary condition of each marker come from a .cfg next to the mesh. No solution fields.

**`xdmf`** (`verified-public-sample`): Unstructured grids and meshio time series are read through meshio; structured topologies (CoRect, Rect, SMesh), spatial collections and dolfinx / ParaView temporal collections through VTK's Xdmf2 reader. FiniteElementFunction (dolfinx checkpoint) attributes are not evaluated: only the mesh of such files is read. Cell-centred data of regular grids is averaged to the grid nodes.

## Getting the data out

**`exodus`**: MOOSE: [Outputs] exodus = true. Sierra/SEACAS/Cubit/libMesh write .e/.exo/.g directly; join parallel pieces (file.e.N.i) with SEACAS epu first.

**`gmsh`**: Gmsh: File > Export > .msh (version 4.1 or 2.2; tick 'Save all elements' only if you have no physical groups). Post-processing views: Save 'Mesh-based' views into the .msh; parsed-view .pos files must be re-saved that way.

**`med`**: Code_Aster: IMPR_RESU(FORMAT='MED', RESU=_F(RESULTAT=...)); Salome: File > Export > MED; Code_Saturne: writer format 'MED'. MED 2.1 files need Salome's medimport.

**`meshio`**: These are mesh formats: results usually live elsewhere (FUN3D: Tecplot/VTK, NGSolve: VTK, FEniCS: XDMF/PVD). Any other meshio format can be converted with `meshio convert in.xxx out.vtu` and read by the vtk connector.

**`su2`**: The .su2 file is the mesh only. SU2 results are written as VTU/PVD (OUTPUT_FILES= PARAVIEW), Tecplot, CSV (surface_flow.csv, restart_flow.csv) or CGNS: read those with the vtk, tecplot, tabular or cgns connectors.

**`xdmf`**: dolfinx: XDMFFile.write_mesh / write_function(u, t); legacy FEniCS: XDMFFile.write; ParaView: Save Data as Xdmf. Keep the .h5 heavy-data file next to the .xdmf.

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0. Installs `meshio>=5.3`, `vtk>=9.3`, `h5py>=3.10`.

# frontier-connector-palabos

Reads Palabos VTK image output directories (.vti, .vts) with parameters from plbLog.dat.

# frontier-connector-pyfr

Reads PyFR native mesh (.pyfrm) and solution (.pyfrs) files, PyFR <= 2.1 and 3.x. Validated on generated files and on PyFR 3.1 and 2.1 output.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install pyfr
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info pyfr
```

## Status

`verified-synthetic`. Reads PyFR <= 2.1 files (spt_* / soln_* datasets) and PyFR 3.x files (eles / nodes, <prefix>/p<order>-<etype> with 'pts'). A solution becomes a point cloud of solution points (quad, hex, tri, tet, pri; legacy files only quad and hex with Gauss-Legendre or Lobatto points; no pyramids, no region subsets); a mesh alone becomes a linear corner mesh. Validated on generated files and on PyFR 3.1 and 2.1 output.

## Getting the data out

PyFR writes soln-<t>.pyfrs next to the .pyfrm mesh; read them directly as a cloud of solution points, or run `pyfr export mesh.pyfrm soln.pyfrs out.vtu` and read the VTU with the vtk connector when cell connectivity is needed.

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0. Installs `h5py>=3.10`.

# frontier-connector-tabular

Reads CSV, TSV and text tables, Parquet, and OpenFOAM probes and force coefficients. Parquet needs pyarrow.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install tabular
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info tabular
```

## Status

`verified-public-sample`. Layouts: point snapshot, long (time, probe) tables, time + signal columns. Global signals are stored on one point at the origin. Parquet needs pyarrow. ParaView, Fluent, CFX and COMSOL style tables and Parquet are validated on generated files only. Tecplot ASCII and COMSOL '% Model:' files belong to their own connectors. Date-string time columns and ragged probe series (without per_probe) are not supported.

## Getting the data out

ParaView: File > Save Data > CSV (point data). Fluent: File > Export > ASCII, or report-file monitors (.out). CFX / COMSOL / STAR-CCM+: export monitor or probe tables as CSV/text. OpenFOAM: the probes and forceCoeffs function objects write postProcessing/<name>/<time>/ files that are read directly.

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0.

| Optional package | Licence | Used to | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pyarrow` | Apache-2.0 | read Parquet |  |

# frontier-connector-vtk

Reads VTK XML, legacy and VTKHDF files, and PVD and .series time series.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install vtk
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info vtk
```

## Getting the data out

ParaView: File > Save Data (.vtu/.vtm, or .pvd with 'Write time series'). OpenFOAM: foamToVTK. SU2/Palabos/Flow360/Luminary/SimScale write VTU directly.

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0. Installs `vtk>=9.3`.

connectors.name: ParaView Catalyst 2 / in-situ streams (Conduit Blueprint spool, relay, ADIOS2)
connectors.export_help: Get the solver-side scripts with `python -m frontier_connectors plugins install exporter-catalyst`, then use one of: (1) copy frontier_emit.py (numpy only) next to the solver and call Emitter.write_step(step, time, blueprint_mesh) at each output step; (2) run the Catalyst 2 pipeline frontier_catalyst_pipeline.py (CATALYST_IMPLEMENTATION_NAME=paraview), which writes the same spool; (3) write Conduit relay Blueprint files (relay.io.blueprint.save_mesh, Ascent) or ADIOS2 BP5 / SST with Blueprint paths as variable names. Follow the run with `python -m frontier_connectors import catalyst <spool|stream> --out ds`. Files a Catalyst pipeline writes with plain VTK extractors (.vtpd / .vtm series, VTKHDF) are read by the `vtk` connector.
connectors.note: Reads frontier-spool directories, Conduit relay Blueprint files (hdf5, json, yaml, conduit_*) and ADIOS2 BP4 / BP5 files and BP5 / SST streams, during or after the run. Validated with Conduit 0.9.5 and ADIOS2 2.12.1. Not validated against ParaView Catalyst (the pipeline script), Fides or MPI-parallel writers.

connectors.name: CGNS (HDF5 natively with h5py; ADF through VTK)
connectors.license: Apache-2.0 (reader: h5py, BSD-3; ADF fallback: VTK, BSD-3)
connectors.export_help: Export CGNS from the solver or post-processor (Ansys CFX: cfx5export -cgns; Fluent: File > Export > CGNS; STAR-CCM+: File > Export > CGNS; Fidelity/FINE, SU2, elsA, Pointwise write it natively) and point at the .cgns file or a directory holding a numbered series.
connectors.note: Reads CGNS/HDF5 with h5py: structured and unstructured zones, linear and quadratic elements, MIXED, NGON_n / NFACE_n, boundary patches as surface zones, vertex and cell-centred solutions, rind, links, FlowSolutionPointers, file-per-step series, units, reference state and flow equations. Cubic and higher elements, face-centred solutions and non-Cartesian coordinates are not supported. ADF files and options={'engine': 'vtk'} go through VTK's vtkCGNSReader, without the CGNS metadata.

connectors.name: code_saturne (EnSight Gold / MED in RESU/<run>/postprocessing)
connectors.vendor: EDF (open source, GPL solver; open output formats)
connectors.license: Apache-2.0 (no vendor code; delegates to open-format readers)
connectors.export_help: No export step: code_saturne writes EnSight Gold by default into RESU/<run>/postprocessing/ (RESULTS_FLUID_DOMAIN.case; MED or CGNS when selected in the writer settings). Point at the case directory, the run directory or the .case; setup.xml and run_solver.log next to postprocessing/ supply the physics.
connectors.note: Reads RESU/<run>/postprocessing output (code_saturne 9.1, FVM 0.3): mesh including polyhedra, cell fields, solver version, turbulence model, fluid properties, notebook variables and boundary natures. Transient EnSight output and the MED and CGNS writers are validated on generated files only.

connectors.name: EnSight Gold / EnSight 6 case
connectors.export_help: Export 'EnSight Gold' from the solver (STAR-CCM+: File > Export or the shipped macro; Fluent: File > Export > EnSight Case Gold; CONVERGE: post_convert; OpenFOAM: foamToEnsight) and point at the .case file.
connectors.note: Reads ASCII, C binary and Fortran binary files: unstructured and structured parts, several time sets, moving geometry. Parts of the highest dimension are read by default, boundary parts with zones=[...]. Server-of-servers (.sos) files are not read.

connectors.name: Exodus II (Sandia SEACAS, MOOSE, libMesh, Cubit, Sierra)
connectors.export_help: MOOSE: [Outputs] exodus = true. Sierra/SEACAS/Cubit/libMesh write .e/.exo/.g directly; join parallel pieces (file.e.N.i) with SEACAS epu first.
connectors.note: Element blocks are the default zones; side sets and node sets are extra zones. Reads nodal, element and global variables at all time steps. One piece of a parallel decomposition is read as it is, without merging.

connectors.name: Geometry only (STL, OBJ, PLY, OFF; STEP / IGES / BREP via optional tessellator)
connectors.license: Apache-2.0 (optional CAD tessellators: cadquery-ocp Apache-2.0 on OpenCascade LGPL-2.1-with-exception; gmsh GPL-2.0-or-later, opt-in only)
connectors.export_help: Any CAD or meshing tool exports STL / OBJ / PLY. For STEP / IGES / BREP install cadquery-ocp (pip install cadquery-ocp) and tune options tessellation={'linear_deflection': ..., 'angular_deflection': ...}. Put a design sweep in one directory to convert it as one dataset.
connectors.note: STL, OBJ, PLY and OFF are read with built-in parsers. STEP, IGES and BREP need cadquery-ocp, or gmsh on request. OBJ materials and textures, PLY tristrips and binary STL colour attributes are ignored.

connectors.name: Gmsh MSH (2.2 / 4.1, ASCII and binary)
connectors.vendor: Gmsh (C. Geuzaine, J.-F. Remacle; open format)
connectors.export_help: Gmsh: File > Export > .msh (version 4.1 or 2.2; tick 'Save all elements' only if you have no physical groups). Post-processing views: Save 'Mesh-based' views into the .msh; parsed-view .pos files must be re-saved that way.
connectors.note: Physical groups become zones. $NodeData and $ElementData views are read, including several time steps of one view; element views assume the consecutive element tags Gmsh writes. $ElementNodeData and .pos parsed views are not read. MSH 4 files need every saved entity in a physical group. Views and binary files are validated on generated files only.

connectors.name: Generic HDF5 (dimension scales, PDEBench / The Well / mesh layouts, mapping config)
connectors.export_help: Write the arrays with h5py / HDF5 from any solver or script, then describe the layout with a mapping config (--mapping file.json) unless it is one of the auto-detected layouts (dimension scales, PDEBench, The Well, points+cells+fields).
connectors.note: Detects datasets with dimension scales, The Well, PDEBench / FNO-style grids and points + cells mesh layouts. Any other layout needs a mapping config: the error prints the dataset tree and a mapping skeleton. The Well, dimension-scale and mesh layouts are validated on generated files only. Fluent CFF, CGNS, MATLAB v7.3, VTKHDF, Exodus, XDMF heavy data, MED and PyFR files belong to their own connectors.

connectors.name: MED (Salome, Code_Aster, Code_Saturne)
connectors.export_help: Code_Aster: IMPR_RESU(FORMAT='MED', RESU=_F(RESULTAT=...)); Salome: File > Export > MED; Code_Saturne: writer format 'MED'. MED 2.1 files need Salome's medimport.
connectors.note: Groups (families) become zones; node groups are point-cloud zones. Reads fields on nodes and cells for every stored time step. Gauss-point (ELGA) and element-node (ELNO) fields are averaged per cell; their storage order for more than one cell is not validated on a real file. Fields on a profile are NaN outside it. Structured MED meshes and polyhedra are not read. Several time steps are validated on generated files only.

connectors.name: Other meshio formats (Medit, Netgen, TetGen, UGRID, MOAB, FLAC3D, PERMAS, ...)
connectors.export_help: These are mesh formats: results usually live elsewhere (FUN3D: Tecplot/VTK, NGSolve: VTK, FEniCS: XDMF/PVD). Any other meshio format can be converted with `meshio convert in.xxx out.vtu` and read by the vtk connector.
connectors.note: Reads Medit .mesh / .meshb, Netgen .vol, TetGen .node / .ele, UGRID and FLAC3D .f3grid. Region and material ids become zones. MOAB .h5m, DOLFIN XML, AVS-UCD, PERMAS, Kratos .mdpa and HMF are validated on meshio-written files only.

connectors.name: Nek5000 / NekRS field files (.f%05d, .nek5000)
connectors.license: Apache-2.0 (own reader; Nek5000 itself is BSD-3)
connectors.export_help: Nek5000 and NekRS write case0.f00001, case0.f00002, ... directly (plus case.nek5000 from the visnek script); point the connector at any of them or at the .nek5000 file.
connectors.note: Reads binary #std files: 2-D and 3-D, single and double precision, both byte orders, split dumps (nfiles > 1); geometry is reused when later dumps omit X. Legacy .fld files and pressure on the PN-2 mesh are not read. Spectral elements are exported as linear GLL sub-cells.

connectors.name: NetCDF 3/4 (CF conventions, UGRID 2-D), optional xarray engine
connectors.license: Apache-2.0 (readers: h5py BSD-3, scipy BSD-3; optional xarray Apache-2.0)
connectors.export_help: Most climate/ocean/weather models and many CFD codes write NetCDF directly; from Python use xarray.Dataset.to_netcdf, from ParaView/VisIt use the NetCDF writer. OPeNDAP URLs, GRIB and multi-file datasets go through options={'engine': 'xarray'}.
connectors.note: NetCDF-4 is read with h5py, NetCDF-3 classic and 64-bit-offset with scipy (memory-mapped). CF grids with 1-D coordinates and UGRID 2-D face meshes are detected automatically. Curvilinear grids, CDF-5, UGRID 1-D / 3-D-layered and DSG feature types need a mapping or options={'engine': 'xarray'}.

connectors.name: OpenFOAM case (Foundation, ESI, foam-extend)
connectors.license: Apache-2.0 (own FoamFile parser; mesh assembly by VTK, BSD-3)
connectors.export_help: Point at the case directory (system/, constant/polyMesh, time directories), a .foam stub inside it or system/controlDict. Decomposed cases (processor*/) are read directly; run reconstructPar first for the collated format (processors<N>/).
connectors.note: Reads ASCII, binary and gzip cases, serial and decomposed (uncollated), with moving points; multi-region with options={'region': ...}. Zones: internalMesh (default) and patch/<name> (opt-in). Steady-solver cases read the last iteration unless options={'iterations': 'all'}. Not read: surface (flux) fields, lagrangian clouds, cell and face zones, collated decomposition.

connectors.name: Palabos (writes VTK .vti/.vtk directly)
connectors.vendor: University of Geneva / FlowKit (open source, AGPL solver; open output format)
connectors.license: Apache-2.0 (no vendor code; delegates to open-format readers)
connectors.export_help: No export step: Palabos writes VTK image data (VtkImageOutput2D/3D -> tmp/vtk*.vti, VtkStructuredImageOutput -> .vts). Point at the output directory (the one holding plbLog.dat) or at a single .vti file.
connectors.note: Reads Palabos output directories (.vti series and .vts states) with Re, resolution, relaxation frequency, dx and dt from plbLog.dat. An output directory is recognised by plbLog.dat next to its VTK files; file numbers are iterations, converted to time with the log's dt, and values are in the units the application wrote. The XML parameter file is not read. 3-D volume series with a log, parallel .pvti and sparse multi-block output are not validated.

connectors.name: PyFR native mesh and solution (.pyfrm, .pyfrs)
connectors.vendor: PyFR (open source, Imperial College London / Texas A&M)
connectors.license: Apache-2.0 (own reader; PyFR itself is BSD-3)
connectors.export_help: PyFR writes soln-<t>.pyfrs next to the .pyfrm mesh; read them directly as a cloud of solution points, or run `pyfr export mesh.pyfrm soln.pyfrs out.vtu` and read the VTU with the vtk connector when cell connectivity is needed.
connectors.note: Reads PyFR <= 2.1 files (spt_* / soln_* datasets) and PyFR 3.x files (eles / nodes, <prefix>/p<order>-<etype> with 'pts'). A solution becomes a point cloud of solution points (quad, hex, tri, tet, pri; legacy files only quad and hex with Gauss-Legendre or Lobatto points; no pyramids, no region subsets); a mesh alone becomes a linear corner mesh. Validated on generated files and on PyFR 3.1 and 2.1 output.

connectors.name: SU2 native mesh (.su2) with its .cfg
connectors.export_help: The .su2 file is the mesh only. SU2 results are written as VTU/PVD (OUTPUT_FILES= PARAVIEW), Tecplot, CSV (surface_flow.csv, restart_flow.csv) or CGNS: read those with the vtk, tecplot, tabular or cgns connectors.
connectors.note: Reads the mesh, markers as boundary zones and multi-zone meshes; solver, turbulence model, free-stream parameters and the boundary condition of each marker come from a .cfg next to the mesh. No solution fields.

connectors.name: Tabular point data (CSV / TSV / text, Parquet, OpenFOAM probes and force coeffs)
connectors.export_help: ParaView: File > Save Data > CSV (point data). Fluent: File > Export > ASCII, or report-file monitors (.out). CFX / COMSOL / STAR-CCM+: export monitor or probe tables as CSV/text. OpenFOAM: the probes and forceCoeffs function objects write postProcessing/<name>/<time>/ files that are read directly.
connectors.note: Layouts: point snapshot, long (time, probe) tables, time + signal columns. Global signals are stored on one point at the origin. Parquet needs pyarrow. ParaView, Fluent, CFX and COMSOL style tables and Parquet are validated on generated files only. Tecplot ASCII and COMSOL '% Model:' files belong to their own connectors. Date-string time columns and ragged probe series (without per_probe) are not supported.

connectors.name: VTK (XML, legacy, VTKHDF, PVD/series time series)
connectors.export_help: ParaView: File > Save Data (.vtu/.vtm, or .pvd with 'Write time series'). OpenFOAM: foamToVTK. SU2/Palabos/Flow360/Luminary/SimScale write VTU directly.

connectors.name: XDMF (FEniCS/dolfinx, Firedrake, PETSc, MOOSE, ParaView)
connectors.export_help: dolfinx: XDMFFile.write_mesh / write_function(u, t); legacy FEniCS: XDMFFile.write; ParaView: Save Data as Xdmf. Keep the .h5 heavy-data file next to the .xdmf.
connectors.note: Unstructured grids and meshio time series are read through meshio; structured topologies (CoRect, Rect, SMesh), spatial collections and dolfinx / ParaView temporal collections through VTK's Xdmf2 reader. FiniteElementFunction (dolfinx checkpoint) attributes are not evaluated: only the mesh of such files is read. Cell-centred data of regular grids is averaged to the grid nodes.

connectors.name: Zarr v2/v3 (xarray-style stores, mapping config, frontier-dataset round trip)
connectors.export_help: xarray: Dataset.to_zarr(path). Any zarr group written by a solver or script can be described with a mapping config. A frontier-dataset directory (or one of its sample stores) is read back as-is.
connectors.note: Reads directory and .zip stores in Zarr v2 and v3. Dimension names come from _ARRAY_DIMENSIONS (v2) or dimension_names (v3); CF attributes are honoured as for NetCDF. Remote stores (s3://, gs://) are not opened. Validated on generated files only.
